title_en: Tianping Auto Insurance Co., Ltd., Suzhou Central Branch v. Wang Kezhong — dispute over the right of recourse
ruling_gist_en: Article 22 of the Regulations on Compulsory Traffic Accident Liability Insurance for Motor Vehicles (hereinafter referred to as the Compulsory Traffic Insurance Regulations) stipulates that for road traffic accidents caused by the following three circumstances, the insurance company shall bear the responsibility of advance payment within the liability limit of the compulsory traffic insurance and has the right to claim recourse against the injurer, namely: (1) the driver does not have a driving qualification or is intoxicated; (2) the insured motor vehicle causes an accident during the period of theft or robbery; (3) the insured intentionally causes a road traffic accident. The escape of a motor vehicle driver after causing an accident is not included within the scope of the above clauses and should not be handled by applying this provision.

full_text_en:
Tianping Automobile Insurance Co., Ltd. Suzhou Central Sub-branch v. Wang Kezhong — dispute over right of recourse

【Ruling Summary】

Article 22 of the Compulsory Traffic Accident Liability Insurance Regulations (hereinafter referred to as the Compulsory Insurance Regulations) provides that in the following three circumstances causing road traffic accidents, the insurance company shall bear the obligation of advance payment within the liability limit of compulsory insurance and shall have the right to seek recourse from the injuring party, namely: (1) the driver did not obtain a driving qualification or was intoxicated; (2) the insured motor vehicle caused an accident during the period of theft or robbery; (3) the insured intentionally caused a road traffic accident. A motor vehicle driver's hit-and-run after an accident is not included within the scope of the above provisions and should not be dealt with by applying such provisions.

Plaintiff: Tianping Automobile Insurance Co., Ltd. Suzhou Central Sub-branch, domiciled at: Donghuan Road, Suzhou Industrial Park, Jiangsu Province.

Defendant: Wang Kezhong, male, Han ethnicity, 42 years old, residing in Suzhou, Jiangsu Province.

Tianping Automobile Insurance Co., Ltd. Suzhou Central Sub-branch (hereinafter referred to as Tianping Insurance Suzhou Company) filed an action with the Wujiang District People's Court of Suzhou, Jiangsu Province, due to a dispute over the right of recourse with Wang Kezhong.

Plaintiff Tianping Insurance Suzhou Company alleged: The defendant Wang Kezhong insured the small car with license plate Su EUXX86 with Tianping Insurance Suzhou Company for compulsory traffic accident liability insurance. On April 28, 2012, Wang Kezhong caused a traffic accident resulting in personal injury and fled the scene. The victim filed a lawsuit with the court claiming compensation. The Wujiang District People's Court of Suzhou rendered Civil Judgment No. (2013) Wujiang Kaimin Chuzi No. 0007, ordering Tianping Insurance Suzhou Company to compensate the victim RMB 76,700 within the scope of compulsory insurance. Tianping Insurance Suzhou Company paid the above amount on April 2, 2013, pursuant to the effective judgment. According to the law, after advancing the relevant expenses within the scope of compulsory insurance, Tianping Insurance Suzhou Company has the right to seek recourse from the party that caused the accident. Since Wang Kezhong refused to pay, Tianping Insurance Suzhou Company filed this lawsuit requesting the court to order Wang Kezhong to return the advanced compensation of RMB 76,700.

Defendant Wang Kezhong argued: The plaintiff Tianping Insurance Suzhou Company has no right of recourse. The Compulsory Traffic Accident Liability Insurance Regulations and the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Cases of Compensation for Damages in Road Traffic Accidents do not list the act of hit-and-run after a traffic accident as a circumstance under which the insurance company can seek recourse. Therefore, the traffic accident in this case falls within the scope of insurance coverage, and Tianping Insurance Suzhou Company does not have the right to seek recourse against Wang Kezhong after paying the compensation. In summary, Wang Kezhong requested the court to dismiss Tianping Insurance Suzhou Company's claims.

The Wujiang District People's Court of Suzhou found at first instance: The defendant Wang Kezhong insured his small car with license plate Su EUXX86 with the plaintiff Tianping Insurance Suzhou Company for compulsory traffic accident liability insurance, with the insurance period from 00:00 on September 21, 2011 to 24:00 on September 20, 2012. At approximately 16:25 on April 28, 2012, Wang Kezhong drove the small car with license plate Su EUXX86 and collided with an electric bicycle driven by Zhang Huaihua (license plate A0XXX33) at the intersection of Lize Road and Wumu Road in Songling Town, Wujiang District, Suzhou, causing Zhang Huaihua to be injured and the vehicles damaged. According to the traffic accident liability determination issued by the traffic police brigade, Wang Kezhong bore full responsibility for the accident, and Zhang Huaihua bore no responsibility. At the same time, the traffic accident liability determination also described the accident process as follows: "After the accident, Wang Kezhong drove away from the scene. The next afternoon, Wang Kezhong surrendered to the public security authorities." On December 21, 2012, Zhang Huaihua filed a lawsuit with the court, demanding that Wang Kezhong and Tianping Insurance Suzhou Company compensate for various losses caused by the traffic accident. The Wujiang District People's Court rendered Civil Judgment No. (2013) Wujiang Kaimin Chuzi No. 0007, ordering Tianping Insurance Suzhou Company to compensate Zhang Huaihua for medical expenses and other losses totaling RMB 76,700 within the scope of compulsory insurance. Subsequently, Tianping Insurance Suzhou Company fulfilled the compensation obligation to Zhang Huaihua.

It was also found that on June 5, 2012, the Traffic Police Patrol Brigade of the Wujiang District Public Security Bureau of Suzhou issued an administrative penalty decision against the defendant Wang Kezhong, imposing a fine of RMB 1,000 for his illegal act of fleeing after causing a traffic accident, which did not constitute a crime. Wang Kezhong did not apply for administrative reconsideration or initiate an administrative lawsuit against the administrative penalty within the prescribed period.

The above facts are confirmed by the following evidence submitted by the plaintiff Tianping Insurance Suzhou Company: insurance policy, road traffic accident liability determination, Civil Judgment No. (2013) Wujiang Kaimin Chuzi No. 0007, payment voucher; evidence obtained by the court: the public security traffic management administrative penalty decision (Wu Gongjiao Jue Zi [2012] No. 320584-2200091154) and notification record, Zhang Huaihua interview record, Wang Kezhong interview record, Pan Hongliang interview record, as well as the in-court statements of both parties.

The Wujiang District People's Court held at first instance: The defendant Wang Kezhong fled the scene after causing the accident, which violated the provisions of relevant Chinese laws, resulting in the loss of some accident evidence and making it impossible for the public security authorities to verify Wang Kezhong's mental and physiological state at the time of the accident. The dangerous nature of this act, compared to circumstances such as not having a driving qualification or drunk driving, shows greater subjective malice and more severe harm to society. The purpose of the state establishing compulsory traffic accident liability insurance is to enable victims to receive compensation according to law and to promote road traffic safety, not to exempt parties responsible for accidents who engage in illegal acts from liability. The Tort Law of the PRC and the Compulsory Traffic Accident Liability Insurance Regulations have already made it clear that in the case of hit-and-run after a motor vehicle accident, the social assistance fund shall first advance the costs of rescue, funeral expenses, etc., for the personal injury of the victim, and then seek recourse from the person responsible for the road accident. Therefore, for the act of hit-and-run after causing an accident, reference should be made to Article 22 of the Compulsory Traffic Accident Liability Insurance Regulations. After the insurance company bears the responsibility of first advancing rescue costs, it has the right to seek recourse from the injuring party, who shall bear the ultimate liability for compensation. In summary, the compulsory traffic accident liability insurance contractual relationship between the parties was legally established and valid. The plaintiff Tianping Insurance Suzhou Company has already compensated the victim within the liability limit of compulsory insurance in accordance with the effective court judgment. Under the circumstance of Wang Kezhong's hit-and-run after causing the accident, Tianping Insurance Suzhou Company has the right to seek recourse from Wang Kezhong for the amount it advanced.

Accordingly, pursuant to Article 5 and Article 23, Paragraph 1 of the Insurance Law of the PRC, and Article 1 and Article 22 of the Compulsory Traffic Accident Liability Insurance Regulations, the Wujiang District People's Court rendered a judgment on August 13, 2013: The defendant Wang Kezhong shall, within ten days after this judgment takes effect, return the advance payment of RMB 76,700 to the plaintiff Tianping Automobile Insurance Co., Ltd. Suzhou Central Sub-branch.

Wang Kezhong, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to the Suzhou Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province, stating: The first-instance judgment misinterpreted the law and applied the law incorrectly. First, the compulsory insurance contract between the parties did not include the circumstance of hit-and-run after a motor vehicle accident as a situation where the insurance company could refuse compensation or seek recourse after compensation. It is not permissible to artificially create a rule or deduce that the insurance company may refuse compensation or seek recourse in the event of a hit-and-run after a traffic accident. Second, according to the provisions of the Compulsory Insurance Regulations, hit-and-run after a traffic accident is not listed as a circumstance for recourse. Furthermore, Article 22 only concerns recourse for advanced rescue costs. In this case, the insurance company did not advance any rescue costs; the dispute concerns compensation for various expenses after the victim suffered disability. Therefore, the insurance company has no right to seek recourse against Wang Kezhong. Third, Article 24 of the Compulsory Insurance Regulations governs the relationship between the relief fund and the person responsible for the traffic accident, not the relationship between the insurance company and the policyholder. It cannot serve as the legal basis for the insurance company to exercise its right of claim against the policyholder. In summary, Wang Kezhong requested the court to set aside the first-instance judgment and amend the judgment according to law.

The appellee Tianping Insurance Suzhou Company argued in the second-instance trial: The first-instance judgment was clear in facts and correct in legal basis. It requested the second-instance court to affirm the judgment according to law.

After the second-instance trial, the Suzhou Intermediate People's Court confirmed the facts found in the first-instance trial.

The Suzhou Intermediate People's Court held in the second-instance trial: Fleeing after a traffic accident is a serious violation of road traffic regulations. According to Article 24 of the Compulsory Traffic Accident Liability Insurance Regulations, the funeral expenses and part or all of the rescue costs for personal injury of the victim in a road traffic accident shall be advanced by the relief fund, and the relief fund management institution has the right to seek recourse from the person responsible for the road traffic accident. This means that the ultimate liability subject for the victim's losses is the party that fled after causing the motor vehicle accident. Therefore, after the appellee Tianping Insurance Suzhou Company fulfilled its compensation obligation to the victim of the traffic accident, it had the right to seek recourse from Wang Kezhong, the injuring party of the insurance accident. The first-instance court's decision ordering the appellant Wang Kezhong to return the advance payment of RMB 76,700 to Tianping Insurance Suzhou Company was not improper. In summary, the first-instance court found the facts clearly, applied the law correctly, and the substantive handling was also proper.

Accordingly, pursuant to Article 170, Paragraph 1, Item (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, the Suzhou Intermediate People's Court rendered a judgment on December 9, 2013: Dismissing the appeal and affirming the original judgment.

Wang Kezhong, dissatisfied with the second-instance judgment, applied to the Jiangsu High People's Court for retrial, stating: The original judgment lacked evidence to prove the main facts and applied the law incorrectly. The compensation under compulsory insurance does not consider the allocation of responsibility for the traffic accident. The law does not provide that after the insurance company undertakes the compensation liability under compulsory insurance, it has the right to seek recourse against the person who caused the accident. There is no corresponding agreement in the insurance policy between the parties in this case. Therefore, even if Wang Kezhong constituted a hit-and-run after a traffic accident, Tianping Insurance Suzhou Company does not have the right of recourse. Accordingly, based on Article 200 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, Wang Kezhong requested a retrial of this case.

After review, the Jiangsu High People's Court rendered a ruling on August 19, 2014: Accepting the retrial of this case.

After the retrial, the Jiangsu High People's Court confirmed the facts found in the first-instance and second-instance trials.

The Jiangsu High People's Court held in the retrial: The appellee Tianping Insurance Suzhou Company claimed that because the retrial applicant Wang Kezhong fled after causing the traffic accident, by reference to Article 22 and Article 24 of the Compulsory Traffic Accident Liability Insurance Regulations of the State Council, it had the right to seek recourse against Wang Kezhong after bearing the insurance compensation liability. In this regard, first, Article 22 of the Compulsory Traffic Accident Liability Insurance Regulations does not include hit-and-run after a traffic accident as a circumstance in which the insurance company enjoys the right of recourse, nor does it provide that other circumstances may be applied by reference. Article 24 only provides for the right of recourse of the social assistance fund and does not provide that the insurance company enjoys the right of recourse. Therefore, Tianping Insurance Suzhou Company's argument that the above provisions should apply is unfounded. Second, Article 53 of the Tort Law of the PRC provides: "If the driver of a motor vehicle flees after a traffic accident and the motor vehicle is covered by compulsory insurance, the insurance company shall compensate within the liability limit of the motor vehicle compulsory insurance; if the motor vehicle is unknown or is not covered by compulsory insurance, and costs for rescue, funeral expenses, etc., for personal injury of the infringed person need to be paid, such costs shall be advanced by the road traffic accident social assistance fund. After the road traffic accident social assistance fund has advanced the costs, its management institution has the right to seek recourse from the person responsible for the traffic accident." This provision sets out different rights and obligations for the insurance company and the social assistance fund, indicating the attitude of national legislation to treat the insurance company and the social assistance fund differently. Third, the funds of the social assistance fund management institution come from administrative allocations or social donations, and the payment of rescue costs to traffic accident victims is made without compensation, whereas the funds of the insurance company come from premiums paid by policyholders, and the payment to victims by the insurance company constitutes performance of insurance contract obligations and is compensated. Therefore, the insurance company should not enjoy the right of recourse that the social assistance fund management institution has. In fact, hit-and-run occurs after the traffic accident, does not increase the probability or risk of the insured accident occurring, and has no connection with the occurrence of the accident itself. Therefore, it is fundamentally different from the circumstances in which the insurance company enjoys the right of recourse as provided in Article 22 of the Compulsory Insurance Regulations. The original judgment, based on Article 24 of the Compulsory Traffic Accident Liability Insurance Regulations, supported Tianping Insurance Suzhou Company's claim for recourse, which contravenes the legislative intent of the Compulsory Insurance Regulations and also contradicts Article 53 of the Tort Law. This constitutes an incorrect application of the law and should be corrected according to law.

Accordingly, pursuant to Article 144, Article 170, Paragraph 1, Item (2), Article 174, and Article 207, Paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, the Jiangsu High People's Court rendered a judgment on December 9, 2014:

1. Setting aside Civil Judgment No. (2013) Suzhong Shang Zhong Zi No. 0754 of the Suzhou Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province and Civil Judgment No. (2013) Wujiang Shang Chu Zi No. 0660 of the Wujiang District People's Court of Suzhou;

2. Dismissing the claims of Tianping Automobile Insurance Co., Ltd. Suzhou Central Sub-branch.

This judgment is final.
